record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports downstream benchmark accuracy for Qwen base models at two parameter counts, providing a limited, indirect test of V6. It does not measure pretraining loss or test power-law scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper's main experiments evaluate prompting on MATH, GSM8K, and Game of 24. Only the Qwen benchmark accuracy results across model sizes bear on V6. The paper's Game of 24 results and its other prompt-performance results do not test the stated scaling-law claim. Results from cited work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a prompting-method paper (Meta Prompting) evaluated on MATH, GSM8K and Game of 24. It does not measure pretraining loss, fit or test any scaling relation, or vary scale as an experimental factor. The Qwen-14B versus Qwen-72B entries are incidental context for the prompting results. Two sizes from one model family, which differ in more than size, cannot show whether downstream performance improves 'predictably' with scale (V6). The paper does not cite or rely on the scaling-law originals. It neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors present the MATH and GSM8K results as proof-of-concept, 'competitive results for Qwen base models' under one fixed structure-only prompt. They say Game of 24 is a batch program-synthesis workflow that is not matched to IO, CoT or ToT. They call for controlled ablations, reproducible evaluators and matched comparisons. They draw no conclusion about scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates prompt methods on downstream math benchmarks; it does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, or optimize training compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that results can depend on model and template; only one fixed task-specific template per benchmark is used in the main experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the Qwen base family, accuracy is higher at 72B than 14B on MATH (MP 28.9 to 46.3) and GSM8K (MP 64.8 to 83.5). This is an uncontrolled two-size comparison inside a prompting study.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger models in a family score higher on math benchmarks under a fixed prompt (monotonic size effect, not predictability).

record.problems: The paper reports only two Qwen base-model sizes for these benchmark comparisons and does not fit or validate a scale-prediction relationship. It states that cross-model comparisons can differ in training data, prompts, decoding, and evaluators; item-level intervals do not capture decoding randomness, prompt-selection uncertainty, evaluator error, or model-choice uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-related results were reported. Cited comparison results and the Game of 24 prompting/resource results were excluded because they do not measure the scaling behavior in the claim.

untested.parts: All: no fitted laws or extrapolation.
All: no other modalities or regimes studied for scaling.
Predictability of downstream performance with scale or loss. Only two model sizes are incidentally reported, with no fit or prediction.
All: no exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The record over-reads incidental two-size accuracy differences as a limited test of V6. The paper never frames model size as a variable of interest. Table 1 also lists Qwen-14B CoT 24.8% and Qwen-72B CoT 35.2% on MATH, which no row records; since the study does not test the claim, these are not listed as missing.

rows.subject: Qwen-14B (base)
rows.operation_detail: Reports MATH pass@1 accuracy for Qwen base models at different parameter counts using the MP evaluation.
rows.note: The table reports this value for the Qwen-14B base model with MP. It is lower than the reported Qwen-72B base MP result (r2), but the paper does not fit or test a predictive scale relationship.
rows.check: Single-model MP accuracy on MATH (28.9%, Table 1). This is a prompting result, not a scaling measurement, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: Qwen-72B (base)
rows.operation_detail: Reports MATH pass@1 accuracy for Qwen base models at different parameter counts using the MP evaluation.
rows.note: The paper identifies 46.3% as its Qwen-72B base MP result; the paired 14B MP table entry is 28.9%. This comparison is not a fitted prediction.
rows.check: Qwen-72B MP on MATH (46.3%) is the paper's headline prompting result. The 14B-to-72B gap is a two-point, uncontrolled comparison and is not a test of predictable scaling. The state should not be 'observed' for V6.

rows.note: The paired Qwen base-model rows are described as the most direct within-model comparison; the 72B MP result is recorded in r4.
rows.check: Single-model MP accuracy on GSM8K (64.8%, Table 2). This is a prompting result, not a scaling measurement.

rows.subject: Qwen-72B (base)

rows.note: Accuracy is higher than the paired Qwen-14B base MP entry. This is a two-size comparison, not a prediction from a fitted scaling relationship.
rows.check: Two-size comparison (64.8% to 83.5%). It contains no fit and no prediction, so it cannot show predictability with scale.
